domain: SaaS revenue recovery and reconciliation. A growth-stage SaaS billing platform where customers pay monthly or annually for starter/pro/enterprise plans. The Postgres database holds the internal source-of-truth (customers, subscriptions, invoices, payments, plus internal risk_flags set by CSMs and support_notes from the support team). Stripe holds the external truth — payment intents, refunds, real subscription state. The two can drift: cards expire, subscriptions cancel in Stripe before Postgres catches up, accidental double-charges happen. The agent's job is to investigate MRR drops by reconciling both sides, then execute recovery actions (retry failed payments, issue refunds, send dunning) in Stripe with operator approval.

personas.name: growth-stage-leak
personas.description: 100-customer growth-stage SaaS, 12 weeks of billing history, three plans (starter $29/mo, pro $99/mo, enterprise $499/mo). The most recent week shows a -$4,820 MRR delta with five distinct causes that must be discoverable in the data: (1) eight failed charges this week — four cards expired this calendar month with new expiries unset, two insufficient_funds declines that historically retry well, two lost_card declines that should not be retried; (2) three enterprise customers downgraded from $499 to $99/mo on the same day after a renewal price-change conversation, captured in support_notes tagged 'downgrade'; (3) two voluntary cancellations this week — both customers had risk_flags of type 'billing_dispute' or 'competitor_mentioned' set 18-21 days earlier by their CSM, with a corresponding support_note explaining the concern, and nobody acted on the flag; (4) one accidental double-charge on customer 'Klein Records' on 2026-04-29 — same amount, same day, two payment intents both succeeded, eligible for a single refund of the duplicate; (5) one drift case — customer 'Larkspur Inc' has Postgres status='active' and mrr_cents=9900, but the Stripe subscription was cancelled 9 days ago and Postgres never picked it up (the cancellation_reason on the Postgres subscription is null). Beyond the affected customers, the wider customer base is healthy: stable MRR over the prior 11 weeks, mix of monthly and annual subscriptions, normal mix of paid and pending invoices, ~6 risk_flags total (some resolved, some active), ~34 support_notes spanning billing complaints, feature requests, and CSM check-ins. Every Stripe customer has a matching Postgres row except for 3 deliberate Stripe-only orphans from a botched import 4 weeks ago. Card BINs on the failed charges should cluster believably (real-shape BIN prefixes). All numbers must reconcile: the MRR delta computed from subscription history matches the sum of the five causes.
